title: Scalar compatibility of compatible degree-one root-chart changes
statement: Let P be a finite purity setting as in [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts], with coefficient prime ell, algebraically closed base field k, and positive levels 1 <= m <= n. Let T be any k-scheme. For primitive ell^n-th roots zeta and zeta-prime, let eta and eta-prime be their ell^(n-m)-th powers, primitive of order ell^m. Let c_zeta and c_zeta-prime be the inverse degree-one root-line charts after shift by 2, ordinary-to-pro-etale comparison inverse image and intrinsic realization, including their canonical shift isomorphisms; define d_eta and d_eta-prime similarly at level m. Using the coefficient unit of [def-pur-smooth-trace] and the shift comparison of [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons], for every morphism a from red_T(A_T[2]) to (A_m)_T[2], red_T(c_zeta^(-1) followed by c_zeta-prime) followed by a equals a followed by d_eta^(-1) followed by d_eta-prime. This is a compatibility of changes of chart, not an existence assertion for a comparison of Tate lines. No finite-type or boundedness hypothesis on T is imposed.

source.place: Step 2: compatibility with the invertible twist; Step 3: reduction of the Kummer line

proof.text: Choose c with zeta = zeta_prime^c using IsPrimitiveRoot.eq_pow_of_pow_eq_one. The two given compatibility equations and pow_right_comm give eta = eta_prime^c. No inverse scalar or coprimality calculation is needed.

Apply finiteReductionRootTrivialization_inv_power at each level. The single-complex functor, shift, comparison inverse image, and intrinsic realization preserve natural-number multiples. The shift comparisons do not depend on the chosen root. Thus the transported chart hom at zeta_prime is c times that at zeta, and the chart hom at eta_prime is c times that at eta.

Finite reduction is additive because it is the left adjoint of the additive restriction functor. Substitute the two hom formulas. The inverse followed by its own chart hom cancels, so each chart change is c times the identity. Functor.map_nsmul and bilinearity of composition reduce both sides of the required equation to c times a. This includes identity reduction, ramified levels, and empty schemes.

proof_origin.source: Transport the existing ordinary root-line power transition through the specified chart functors, then cancel to natural-number multiples of identities; finite-reduction proof Steps 2--3.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteReductionLineChart_scalars (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ P.level)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [T.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (a : (P.finiteReduction m hm hmn T).obj ((P.coefficientUnit T)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ⟶
      ((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).coefficientUnit T)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)
    (ζ η ζ' η' : P.field.k)
    (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ P.diagonalExponent)
    (hη : IsPrimitiveRoot η (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).diagonalExponent)
    (hζ' : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ' P.diagonalExponent)
    (hη' : IsPrimitiveRoot η' (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).diagonalExponent)
    (h : η = ζ ^ (P.coefficients.l ^ (P.level - m)))
    (h' : η' = ζ' ^ (P.coefficients.l ^ (P.level - m))) :
    (P.finiteReduction m hm hmn T).map
        ((P.finiteReductionLineChart T ζ hζ).inv ≫
          (P.finiteReductionLineChart T ζ' hζ').hom) ≫ a =
      a ≫ ((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionLineChart T η hη).inv ≫
        ((P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionLineChart T η' hη').hom
